issue.title: Bug: [CmisManagerTask] Potential race condition between split ports while doing DPSM

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

DPSM might enter Failed state due to race condition in CmisManagerTask. For example, there is 1 module split to 2 logical ports: Ethernet0 with lane(0,1,2,3) and Ethernet4 with lane(4,5,6,7). At the beginning, both ports are admin down.Think about following flow:
1. User set Ethernet0 to admin up. CmisManagerTask starts DPSM for Ethernet0. The DPSM put the module into high power and then to ModuleReady
2. User set Ethernet4 to admin up. CmisManagerTask starts DPSM for Ethernet4. Etherent4 calls force disable, set timeout to "txoff_duration" and enter "CMIS_STATE_DP_PRE_INIT_CHECK". In this case, the txoff_duration is 0.05s.
3. According to CMIS standard, module should start default hardware initialization if module is in ModuleReady state and its datapath is not explicitly deinited (by calling api.set_datapath_deinit in sonic). So, Ethernet4 goes to hardware initialization and transite to  "DataPathInit" state.
4. However, CmisManagerTask expects Ethernet4 to be "DataPathInitialized" or "DataPathDeactivated" state in **0.05s**. Ethernet4 will be in "DataPathInit" state for a few seconds and failed all the retry.

The issue is found on following module:

```
        Vendor Name: FINISAR CORP.
        Vendor OUI: 00-90-65
        Vendor PN: FCBN950QE2C10-MS
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Split a module into 2 ports
2. The txoff_duration of the module should be small, e.g. 0.5
3. Put 2 ports to admin down
4. Start port1 first. When port1 enter ModuleReady, start port2. (The timing is important)

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual: port2 DPSM failed
Expected: port DPSM pass

resolution.title: [cmis] Fix issue: Potential race condition between split ports while doing DPSM
resolution.description:
## Why I did it

Fix issue: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/27373

CMIS datapath deinitialization should follow the expected software deinit sequence. When forcing a datapath re-init because `host_tx_ready` is false or the port is administratively down, xcvrd should request datapath deinit before disabling media-side Tx.

This keeps the forced re-init path consistent with the normal `CMIS_STATE_DP_DEINIT` flow and CMIS datapath state machine behavior.

## How I did it

Updated the forced re-init path in `cmis_manager_task.py` to call `set_datapath_deinit()` before `tx_disable_channel()`.

Updated the existing `test_CmisManagerTask_task_worker_host_tx_ready_false_to_true` unit test to record the mock API call order and verify that datapath deinit is issued before Tx disable.

## How to verify it

Run the xcvrd unit test:

```bash
python3 -m pytest sonic-xcvrd/tests/test_xcvrd.py -k test_CmisManagerTask_task_worker_host_tx_ready_false_to_true
